lede: Mountain Village Council meets Thursday with a resolution that sets the appreciation cap on deed-restricted units — the fine print that determines whether affordable housing actually stays affordable or quietly drifts out of reach. Elsewhere, it's a heavy week for land use: HARC takes up the Shandoka Lot redevelopment on Black Bear Road and an unpermitted pergola at the Elks Lodge, Telluride P&Z gets its first look at employee housing on the school campus, and Ouray County holds three public hearings including a full repeal of Section 16 of its land use code. Tuesday also marks the first day of school for Telluride R-1.

notable.stake: HARC decides whether to approve an unpermitted structure in the Historic Landmark District.
Preliminary large-scale review of Shandoka Lot redevelopment — four new buildings on Black Bear Road.
Commission recommends 2027 campground and shower fee increases of up to 25%.
BOCC reviews housing authority compliance and holds a public hearing on a land-use application.
Three public hearings including full repeal of Ouray County land use code Section 16.
Public hearings on four special event liquor permits open to public comment.
Resolution sets appreciation cap on deed-restricted units — core to keeping housing affordable.
First formal review of school district employee housing proposal at the high school site.
